summary: List every path from node 0 to node n - 1 in a directed acyclic graph.
mainInsight: Enumerating all paths needs exhaustive search: DFS from 0 with a shared path list, append on entry, record a copy at n - 1, pop on return. Because the graph is acyclic no visited set is needed.
invariant: When dfs(node) runs, path holds exactly the nodes from 0 to node along the current branch.

approaches.name: Backtracking DFS
approaches.summary: DFS from 0 with one mutable path; copy it when reaching n - 1.

approaches.name: BFS over partial paths
approaches.summary: Queue holds paths; extend each by its last node's neighbours.

approaches.name: Memoised DFS (paths from node to target)
approaches.summary: paths(v) = [[v] + p for nxt in graph[v] for p in paths(nxt)].

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def allPathsSourceTarget(self, graph: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
        target = len(graph) - 1
        paths, path = [], [0]

        def dfs(node):
            if node == target:
                paths.append(path[:])      # copy: O(n) per path found
                return
            for nxt in graph[node]:        # DAG: no visited set needed, no cycles
                path.append(nxt)
                dfs(nxt)
                path.pop()                 # backtrack

        dfs(0)                             # up to 2^(n-2) paths, each up to n long
        return paths
commonMistakes: Appending `path` instead of a copy, so every result ends up identical (and empty).
Adding a visited set, which wrongly prunes nodes that appear on several different paths.
Forgetting to pop after the recursive call.
edgeCases: Complete DAG where every i links to every j > i (2^(n-2) paths).

promptVariants: Why does this DFS not need a visited set?
What would a global visited set break here?
options: The graph is a DAG, so no path revisits a node
Each node has at most one incoming edge
n is at most 15, so cycles are short
The adjacency lists contain no duplicates
cards.answer: The graph is a DAG, so no path revisits a node
cards.explanation: Without cycles the search terminates on its own. A global visited set would block a node reached again by a different path, losing valid paths.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Each node has at most one incoming edge: Nodes can have many incoming edges (node 3 in example 1 has two).
incorrectOptionExplanations.n is at most 15, so cycles are short: There are no cycles at all; small n is about output size.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The adjacency lists contain no duplicate: Unique neighbours avoid duplicate paths but do not prevent cycles.

promptVariants: What goes wrong if the base case does `paths.append(path)` instead of `path[:]`?
Why copy the path when it reaches the target?
options: All entries alias one list, emptied to [0] at the end
Only the first path is stored and others are skipped

cards.answer: All entries alias one list, emptied to [0] at the end
cards.explanation: Backtracking pops the shared list, so every stored reference ends up pointing at the final state [0].

incorrectOptionExplanations.Only the first path is stored and others: Every path is appended, but as the same object.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Python raises an error when the list is: Mutating a list stored elsewhere is legal and silent.

cards.explanation: Paths: 0-3, 0-2-3, 0-1-3, 0-1-2-3. Each of the middle nodes 1 and 2 is either in or out: 2^(n-2) = 4.

incorrectOptionExplanations.3: Misses 0-1-2-3, the path through both middle nodes.
incorrectOptionExplanations.8: That is 2^(n-1); the endpoints are always included.

promptVariants: Derive the worst-case time of the canonical code.
Why is the running time exponential, and what is the bound?
cards.answer: In a complete DAG every middle node can be in or out of a path, so there are 2^(n-2) paths, each up to n long. Copying each path costs O(n), and the DFS explores each path prefix once, giving O(2^n * n).
cards.explanation: When the output itself is exponential, the algorithm cannot be faster than the output.

promptVariants: Besides the output, the recursion stack and path use O(___) space.
cards.explanation: The path and recursion depth are at most n because a DAG path visits each node once.
